$comment: Fields Polaris serves to Nova, per response object.
Nova and Polaris ship from separate repositories on separate schedules, and both
sides address these fields by string literal. Nothing in either build can see the
other, so a rename on one side degrades silently: a reader falls back to its
default and the feature quietly stops working rather than failing.
This manifest is the shared record. tests/integration/test_nova_contract.cpp keeps
Polaris honest about it, and scripts/check-nova-contract.py diffs it against a Nova
checkout. Adding a field to a response means adding it here in the same commit.
Drift found when this manifest was introduced, on 2026-08-06, is recorded under
known_drift so it is tracked rather than rediscovered.

game.$comment: Emitted per app by the game library endpoint.

$comment: Scoped to the function, not the file and not the receiver variable.
PolarisGameJsonAdapter.kt defines fromJson, parseArtworkManifest, finiteDouble and
parseArtworkAsset, and all four name their parameter `json`. Scoping by receiver
therefore reports artwork-manifest fields as game fields, which is how an earlier
version of this manifest recorded drift that did not exist.

required_by_nova.$comment: Fields Nova reads. Anything else Polaris serves here is informational.
required_by_nova.note: Nova reads every field this object serves.

launch_mode.$comment: Nested under game, built by build_launch_mode_contract. Aligned in both directions. An earlier revision recorded drift here because the field list was extracted from the thin launch_mode_contract_for_app wrapper, and the range ran on into steam_launch_contract_for_app and reported that object's fields instead.

steam_launch.$comment: Nested under game. The reference case: identical shape to launch_mode and currently aligned in both directions.

$comment: Nested under game. Per-host, computed once per request from the same fallback
display mode the web planner plans from, and attached to every game unchanged.
Nova's adapter reads it since papi-ux/nova#197, and Play Setup's Resolution row
gates on `available`. The shared model's contract test pins the 2560x1600x90
fixture on the Nova side; tests/unit/test_display_planner.cpp pins it here.
Unlike the web planner, `hidden` here means unsafe and nothing else; the
advanced flag is its own axis so a client can offer its own advanced toggle.

display_planner_choice.$comment: One entry of display_planner.choices: a preset of the ported web planner.

$comment: The `capture` object of /polaris/v1/session/status.
Most of this is diagnostic and going unread is not a defect. The exceptions are
called out in informational_ok below.
Nested under session_encoder.selection. This explains the deterministic host-side
Auto policy, its runtime-selected encoder, and whether an exact live probe used the
documented fallback. Nova, Doctor, and the web UI consume the same informational
evidence without giving any surface control over launch behavior.
The `linux_gpu_profile` object of /polaris/v1/session/status.
This is where Nova gets its authoritative GPU-native answer, not from the capture
object, which is why capture.gpu_native and capture.cross_gpu_dmabuf_risk going
unread is redundancy rather than a gap.
The response of GET /polaris/v1/session/timing (Nordstern P0-3, scoped
per-session by P0-3A after a same-day design review found the original
process-lifetime rings could commingle concurrent sessions - Polaris runs
one independent encoder per client, default max_sessions 2). Host-side
T0-T2 stage timing for the calling cert's own session only. No nova_reader
yet: this shipped ahead of any consumer, same situation display_planner was
in before papi-ux/nova#197 - see known_drift.polaris_sends_nova_never_reads
for that precedent. Add nova_reader here once a Nova build actually reads
this endpoint.
One entry of capabilities.modes in GET /polaris/v1/client-settings - the
host-authoritative launch-mode catalog (per-mode availability, server
labels, disable reasons, and the private/host grouping). Guarded because
the client-settings surface carried the picker feed with zero drift
protection (roadmap item: server-authoritative mode pickers). The POST
validator accepts exactly the ids this catalog can advertise as
available - stream_display_policy::selection_valid is the shared truth.
group/unavailable_reason and the runtime/capture/topology vocabulary
ship ahead of their Nova consumer - see known_drift.
One entry of capabilities.encoders in GET /polaris/v1/client-settings and
encoder_backends in GET /polaris/v1/capabilities. Availability describes
what the running build can select; every request is validated again against
the live capture route at launch. Auto alone may fall back.
Top-level GET /optimize deterministic launch resolver response.
append_deterministic_optimization_json emits the selected preset, the
authoritative nested field provenance, and temporary flat compatibility
values. History, recovery records, and AI output cannot define these
settings. ai_explanation is typed informational output only.
The exact session encoder selection nested under encoder_resolution in a
deterministic /optimize response. Nova binds requested, resolved, lock, and
fallback policy to the final launch. The concrete active backend remains
informational because Auto is resolved only by the live launch probe.
Exact app and topology identity bound to a deterministic optimize result.
Nova rejects a preflight or fresh result unless the canonical app id,
host-default or explicit topology request, lock state, and Steam desktop
choice all match the launch that will consume it. Source, reason, and
normalization metadata make paired, app, and host capability decisions
auditable without allowing them to become client-authored policy.
One entry in resolved_profile.fields. Nova rejects the value unless
all provenance metadata is present with the expected primitive types.
A trusted launch envelope requires display_mode plus display_width,
display_height, target_fps, target_bitrate_kbps, and hdr. Component
display provenance is authoritative when a preset composes paired
dimensions with an explicit cadence lock. Source is allowlisted and
history or AI provenance is never accepted as launch authority.
Corrected 2026-08-07. The first version of this file was written against the
working tree of a Nova checkout that was 295 commits divergent from origin/master,
and scoped reads by receiver name rather than by function. Both errors inflated it.
Verified against origin/master with function scoping, Nova reads every field Polaris
serves; only the reverse direction drifts.

nova_reads_polaris_never_sends.$comment: Nova defaults each of these, so platform and runtime resolve to "unknown" and the labels to empty strings rather than failing.

$comment: None. display_planner sat here for the day it was served ahead of its consumer;
papi-ux/nova#197 wired the adapter and the records moved back out, with the
nova_reader entries above repointed at the functions that now read it.

session_capture: Corrected. Nova reads gpu_native_succeeded and cross_gpu_dmabuf_risk from the
linux_gpu_profile object instead, so the same fields on capture are redundant rather
than missed. An earlier revision recorded them as drift because linux_gpu_profile was
linux_gpu_profile: Resolved. Nova read vaapi_vendor and Polaris never served it; vaapi.cpp logged the
string at encoder creation without publishing it. It is now recorded in stats and
served in this object, which is what names the driver generation in a crash report.
game: platform and runtime are now served, derived from the Lutris runner persisted at
import; they are omitted for apps whose runtime is not recorded, which Nova renders
as no badge. The remaining four are deliberate: launcher_source falls back to source
in Nova and would only matter if Polaris distinguished imported-from vs launched-via;
launcher_detail has no host-side value to serve; platform_label and runtime_label
exist so a server can label a value the client cannot map, and every value served
today is one Nova already maps.
optimization: The containment resolver serves resolved_profile directly from deterministic
policy. Remaining top-level compatibility fields are informational only; Nova
requires the typed resolved-profile envelope before they can affect launch.
